summary: This bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to let manufacturers relocating production from abroad to the US treat related nonresidential real property as 20-year property eligible for bonus depreciation, exclude gain on sales of foreign manufacturing assets tied to such moves, and make 100% bonus depreciation permanent for qualified property.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions that authorize, appropriate, or modify any direct government outlays or programs. All changes are to the tax code via depreciation rules and gain exclusions. Therefore it has no bearing on government spending levels.

The bill amends IRC sections 168 and adds new section 139J to create accelerated depreciation, 100% bonus depreciation made permanent, and an exclusion of gain on certain property sales, all explicitly to lower the tax burden on manufacturers that relocate production to the United States. This is a clear, targeted tax reduction.
No provisions address health insurance, providers, Medicare/Medicaid, or any health-related tax credits or regulations.
No provisions relate to firearms, background checks, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address visas, border security, asylum, or immigration enforcement.
No provisions address reproductive health services, funding restrictions, or abortion access.
No provisions affect defense authorizations, appropriations, or military procurement.
No provisions modify environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation programs.
No provisions alter eligibility, funding, or administration of welfare, SNAP, housing assistance, or similar programs.
No provisions address schools, student aid, school choice, or education tax benefits.
No provisions address controlled substances, enforcement priorities, or decriminalization.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or reentry programs.

The core purpose is to incentivize relocation of manufacturing from foreign countries to the United States through tax benefits. This constitutes a deliberate policy favoring domestic production over foreign production and therefore has a protectionist orientation.

By enacting new tax expenditures without offsetting revenue increases or spending cuts, the bill increases the deficit in the near term. This aligns with accepting deficit effects to achieve the policy goal rather than prioritizing immediate debt reduction.
No provisions address nondiscrimination protections, marriage, or LGBTQ-specific legal rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance programs or funding levels.
No provisions address voting procedures, election administration, or campaign finance.
No provisions address data privacy, platform regulation, or technology sector oversight.
No provisions address collective bargaining, union organizing, wage standards, or worker protections.
No provisions address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or conflicts between civil rights and religious liberty.
